newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin wants "more energetic" reforms in Russia.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin wants "more energetic" reforms in Russia.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin said in a radio address on Friday that radical government changes he is making were aimed at "more energetic and consistent reforms than before".
"As you know I have recently delivered my annual address to the Federal Assembly," Yeltsin, 66, said in a clear and confident voice.

"Immediately after that, the first steps were made to implement it, first of all by making changes in the government. I am talking about more energetic and consistent continuation of reforms than before."
Yeltsin has ordered Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and his first deputy, liberal reformer Anatoly Chubais, to form a largely new government.
The new line-up is expected to be announced any day before Yeltsin leaves for a summit with U.S. President Bill Clintion in Helsinki next Wednesday.
Most of Yeltsin's address was devoted to the problems of the Russian media. He promised to support and protect the media, but also appealed for a responsible approach form them.
Later on Friday Yeltsin was due to meet Russian media bosses, whose role will be important in the next stage of reforms.
Some of the decisions the government faces, such as abolishing state subsidies for housing, will be unpopular with millions of people.
Yeltsin will need all the backing he can get from the liberal media, which also helped him secure victory in last year's presidential election.
